module Unison.Runtime.MCode
data Args'
Arg1 :: !Int -> Args'
Arg2 :: !Int -> !Int -> Args'
ArgN :: {-# UNPACK #-} !PrimArray Int -> Args'
ArgR :: !Int -> !Int -> Args'
data Args
ZArgs :: Args
VArg1 :: !Int -> Args
VArg2 :: !Int -> !Int -> Args
VArgR :: !Int -> !Int -> Args
VArgN :: {-# UNPACK #-} !PrimArray Int -> Args
VArgV :: !Int -> Args

-- | Efficient mapping for record field names
newtype FieldRef
FieldRef :: Word64 -> FieldRef

-- | The shape of a record: which fields it has, and where each one sits in
--   a record value's slots.
--   
--   One of these is built per record-construction site and is carried by
--   every value built there. Reaching it from the value is what lets
--   <a>Eq</a> and <tt>compareClosure</tt> -- which are pure, with no
--   access to the code cache -- order two records of *different* shapes by
--   field name. That case is reachable: two records with different fields
--   can be compared once they are wrapped in <tt>Any</tt>, which erases
--   their types.
data RecordShape
RecordShape :: !RecordRef -> !Vector FieldName -> !PrimArray Word64 -> !PrimArray Int -> RecordShape

-- | Interned id for this field set. Not used for ordering: it is handed
--   out in allocation order, which is why ordering goes through
--   <a>shapeFields</a> instead.
[shapeRef] :: RecordShape -> !RecordRef

-- | The record's field names, ascending. Slot <tt>i</tt> of a record value
--   holds the value of <tt>shapeFields ! i</tt>.
[shapeFields] :: RecordShape -> !Vector FieldName

-- | The field numbers (<a>FieldRef</a>), ascending; with <a>shapeSlots</a>
--   the slot of each field, for <a>RecUnpack</a> and <a>RecSet</a>. Two
--   unboxed arrays searched by <a>shapeSlot</a> rather than a map: a
--   lookup is a binary search over a few words, and native code does the
--   same search over the <tt>ByteArray#</tt>s (unison_jit_rec_pos). Built
--   by <a>mkRecordShape</a>.
[shapeKeys] :: RecordShape -> !PrimArray Word64

-- | The slot of the field at the same index of <a>shapeKeys</a>.
[shapeSlots] :: RecordShape -> !PrimArray Int

-- | A shape from its reference, its field names ascending, and the number
--   of each field in that order (so the field at slot <tt>i</tt> has
--   number <tt>refs !! i</tt>).
mkRecordShape :: RecordRef -> Vector FieldName -> [FieldRef] -> RecordShape

-- | The slot of a field in a record of this shape: a binary search of
--   <a>shapeKeys</a>. A field the shape lacks is an error, not a result:
--   typechecked code only reads fields the record has, so there is nothing
--   to recover from, and nothing to allocate on the way out.
shapeSlot :: RecordShape -> FieldRef -> Int

-- | Build the shape for a record schema, assigning a <a>FieldRef</a> to
--   any field name not yet seen.
recordShape :: MonadState RecordFieldMappings m => RecordRef -> RecordSchema -> m RecordShape

-- | Build the shape for a record schema from already-interned field names.
--   Returns Nothing if any of them is unknown, which shouldn't happen for
--   a schema that is itself already interned.
recordShapeFrom :: RecordFieldMappings -> RecordRef -> RecordSchema -> Maybe RecordShape
data RefNums
RN :: (Reference -> Word64) -> (Reference -> Word64) -> (Reference -> Maybe Int) -> (RecordSchema -> RecordRef) -> RefNums
[dnum] :: RefNums -> Reference -> Word64
[cnum] :: RefNums -> Reference -> Word64
[anum] :: RefNums -> Reference -> Maybe Int
[recNum] :: RefNums -> RecordSchema -> RecordRef
data MLit
MI :: !Int -> MLit
MN :: !Word64 -> MLit
MC :: !Char -> MLit
MD :: !Double -> MLit
MT :: !Text -> MLit
MM :: !Referent -> MLit
MY :: !Reference -> MLit
data GInstr comb
Prim2 :: !Prim2 -> !Int -> !Int -> GInstr comb
Lit :: !MLit -> GInstr comb
Prim1 :: !Prim1 -> !Int -> GInstr comb
ForeignCall :: !Bool -> !ForeignFunc -> !Args -> GInstr comb
Pack :: !Reference -> !PackedTag -> !Args -> GInstr comb
Name :: !GRef comb -> !Args -> GInstr comb
RefCAS :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> GInstr comb
DLLCall :: GInstr comb
SetAff :: !Bool -> !Int -> !Int -> GInstr comb
Capture :: !Word64 -> GInstr comb
Discard :: !Int -> GInstr comb
Info :: !String -> GInstr comb
RecPack :: !RecordShape -> !Args -> GInstr comb
RecUnpack :: !Vector FieldRef -> !Int -> GInstr comb
RecSet :: !FieldRef -> !Args -> GInstr comb
Print :: !Int -> GInstr comb
Reset :: !EnumSet Word64 -> !Int -> !Maybe Int -> GInstr comb
InLocal :: !Int -> GInstr comb
Fork :: !Int -> GInstr comb
Atomically :: !Int -> GInstr comb
Seq :: !Args -> GInstr comb
TryForce :: !Int -> GInstr comb
SandboxingFailure :: !Text -> GInstr comb
KeepAlive :: !Int -> GInstr comb
NewForeignPtr :: !Int -> !Int -> GInstr comb
AddFinalizer :: !Int -> !Int -> GInstr comb
MkCallback :: !Int -> !Int -> GInstr comb
type Instr = GInstr CombIx
type RInstr val = GInstr RComb val
data GSection comb
Ins :: !GInstr comb -> !GSection comb -> GSection comb
Call :: !Bool -> !CombIx -> comb -> !Args -> GSection comb
DMatch :: !Maybe Reference -> !Int -> !GBranch comb -> GSection comb
Let :: !GSection comb -> !CombIx -> !Int -> !GSection comb -> !Ptr NativeCell -> GSection comb
Yield :: !Args -> GSection comb
App :: !Bool -> !GRef comb -> !Args -> GSection comb
Jump :: !Int -> !Args -> GSection comb
Match :: !Int -> !GBranch comb -> GSection comb
Die :: String -> GSection comb
Exit :: GSection comb
NMatch :: !Maybe Reference -> !Int -> !GBranch comb -> GSection comb
RMatch :: !Int -> !GSection comb -> !EnumMap Word64 (GBranch comb) -> GSection comb
pattern MatchT :: Int -> GSection comb -> Map Text (GSection comb) -> GSection comb
pattern MatchW :: Int -> GSection comb -> EnumMap Word64 (GSection comb) -> GSection comb
type RSection val = GSection RComb val
type Section = GSection CombIx
data GComb val comb
Comb :: {-# UNPACK #-} !GCombInfo comb -> GComb val comb
CachedVal :: !Word64 -> !val -> GComb val comb

-- | Matches any combinator, ignoring its native code cell. Building one
--   with this gives it the shared "never compiled" cell, so don't use it
--   to rebuild a combinator that already has a cell of its own.
pattern Lam :: Int -> Int -> GSection comb -> GComb val comb
data GCombInfo comb
LamI :: !Int -> !Int -> !GSection comb -> !Ptr NativeCell -> GCombInfo comb

-- | A native code cell (see
--   unison-runtime<i>src</i>Unison<i>Runtime</i>JIT/design.md): the
--   mutable part of a combinator, 32 bytes outside the Haskell heap, never
--   moved and never freed, so generated code can refer to it by address.
--   As a C struct:
--   
--   <pre>
--   struct cell {
--     void    *code;    // offset 0: the compiled entry point, NULL until compiled
--     int64_t  count;   // offset 8: calls made while code was NULL
--     int64_t  state;   // offset 16: 0 not yet requested, 1 queued, 2 taken by the compile thread
--     int64_t  verdict; // offset 24: whether it is worth compiling (see readNativeVerdict)
--   };
--   </pre>
--   
--   The state only moves forward, so a combinator is asked for only once.
--   The layout is a contract between two readers: this module (the <tt>
--   and </tt> accessors below, at those offsets) and the generated code,
--   which loads <tt> at offset 0 to call through a cell and writes </tt>
--   at offset 8 (JIT/Codegen.hs); nothing in the C runtime reads a cell.
--   
--   The count starts at minus the JIT's compilation threshold when the JIT
--   compiles what gets hot, so that "hot" is the count reaching zero: the
--   interpreter's test is one comparison with a constant. A count that
--   starts at zero or above never gets there.
data NativeCell

-- | Reads the compiled code pointer of a cell. Null means "interpret". An
--   atomic (acquire) load: the compile thread writes a module's pool
--   entries and exit and frame tables before it publishes the code
--   pointer, and an interpreter thread that sees the pointer must then see
--   those too, which on a weakly ordered machine (arm64) a plain load does
--   not promise (an <tt>ldar</tt>, a few cycles on an entry that costs
--   tens of nanoseconds).
readNativeCode :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO (Ptr ())

-- | The compiled code the interpreter should enter, if any. Null means
--   "interpret": there is no code, or the function is so small that
--   getting into native code and back costs more than interpreting it
--   (verdict 3; native callers still call it directly).
readNativeEntry :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO (Ptr ())

-- | Installs compiled code. A single atomic (release) pointer write:
--   readers on other threads see either the old value or the new one, and
--   a reader that sees the new one sees everything the compile thread
--   wrote before it (see <a>readNativeCode</a>).
writeNativeCode :: Ptr NativeCell -> Ptr () -> IO ()

-- | Counts a call made while the cell had no compiled code, and says
--   whether that made it hot (the count reached zero). Not atomic; a lost
--   count under contention does not matter.
bumpNativeCount :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO Bool
readNativeCount :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO Int

-- | Sets a cell's count: negative, to make it hot after that many more
--   calls.
writeNativeCount :: Ptr NativeCell -> Int -> IO ()

-- | Marks the cell as requested (state 0 to 1), atomically, and says
--   whether this call was the one that did. Whoever does owns the request,
--   and queues it.
claimNativeCell :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO Bool

-- | Puts the state back to 0: for a request that could not be queued.
releaseNativeCell :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO ()

-- | The compile thread takes the cell (state 2), whether it was requested
--   or not, and says whether this call was the one that did. A combinator
--   that is taken is being compiled, or has been, or can't be. A request
--   found already taken when it comes off the queue is dropped: its
--   combinator went into an earlier batch.
takeNativeCell :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO Bool

-- | Whether a request for the cell is queued.
nativeCellRequested :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO Bool

-- | What the JIT has decided about compiling the cell's combinator. Zero:
--   nothing yet. Otherwise the low two bits say: 1 worth compiling, 2
--   better left to the interpreter, because native code for it would spend
--   its time leaving native code, 3 worth compiling for native callers but
--   too small to be worth entering from the interpreter. The bits above
--   hold an estimate the JIT keeps for judging callers (see JIT.Estimate).
--   Only the thread that compiles writes this; the interpreter reads it
--   when it finds code in the cell.
readNativeVerdict :: Ptr NativeCell -> IO Int
writeNativeVerdict :: Ptr NativeCell -> Int -> IO ()

-- | Cells are handed out from a pool, so that loading code (an STM
--   transaction) never has to allocate memory: a retried transaction would
--   leak it. The pool is a block of cells and a count of how many are in
--   use. When it runs out, a new block is allocated outside the
--   transaction with <a>growNativeCellPool</a>. Old blocks stay in use,
--   and are never freed.
data NativeCellPool
NativeCellPool :: !Ptr NativeCell -> !Int -> !Int -> NativeCellPool

-- | Allocates zeroed cells for <tt>n</tt> combinators, as one block that
--   is never freed.
newNativeCells :: Int -> IO (Ptr NativeCell)

-- | The cell at index <tt>i</tt> of a block from <a>newNativeCells</a>.
nativeCellAt :: Ptr NativeCell -> Int -> Ptr NativeCell
newNativeCellPool :: Int -> Int -> IO NativeCellPool

-- | Takes <tt>n</tt> cells from the pool, or fails if it has fewer left.
takeNativeCells :: Int -> NativeCellPool -> Maybe (Ptr NativeCell, NativeCellPool)

-- | A fresh block with room for at least <tt>n</tt> cells, and at least
--   twice the old capacity so that growing stays rare.
growNativeCellPool :: Int -> Int -> NativeCellPool -> IO NativeCellPool

-- | A shared cell for combinators that are never compiled: builtins, and
--   combinators that were not loaded through the code cache.
noNativeCell :: Ptr NativeCell

-- | Gives every combinator in a group of freshly loaded code its own cell
--   from <tt>base</tt>, numbering them in order. Returns the count used.
attachNativeCells :: Ptr NativeCell -> EnumMap Word64 (GCombs val comb) -> (Int, EnumMap Word64 (GCombs val comb))
type Comb = GComb Void CombIx

-- | The fixed point of a GComb where all references to a Comb are
--   themselves Combs.
newtype RComb val
RComb :: GComb val (RComb val) -> RComb val
[unRComb] :: RComb val -> GComb val (RComb val)
type RCombInfo val = GCombInfo RComb val

-- | Map of combinators, parameterized by comb reference type
type GCombs val comb = EnumMap Word64 GComb val comb
type RCombs val = GCombs val RComb val
data CombIx

data GRef comb

type RRef val = GRef RComb val

-- | A reference to a combinator, parameterized by comb
type Ref = GRef CombIx

data GBranch comb
Test1 :: !Word64 -> {-# UNPACK #-} !Arm comb -> !GSection comb -> GBranch comb
Test2 :: !Word64 -> {-# UNPACK #-} !Arm comb -> !Word64 -> {-# UNPACK #-} !Arm comb -> !GSection comb -> GBranch comb
TestW :: !GSection comb -> !EnumMap Word64 (Arm comb) -> GBranch comb
TestT :: !GSection comb -> !Map Text (GSection comb) -> GBranch comb
TestY :: !GSection comb -> !Map Bytes (GSection comb) -> GBranch comb

-- | A case of a branch: the fields it binds and its code.
data Arm comb
Arm :: !ConstructorArity -> !GSection comb -> Arm comb

-- | How many fields a match arm binds: the number of slots <a>emitCase</a>
--   lays the arm's context out with. A data or request match's arm carries
--   it (<a>Arm</a>), because it is the one thing about an arm that the
--   object being matched cannot say: the interpreter pushes the object's
--   own fields and runs the arm only when their count is the arm's
--   (<tt>dataBranch</tt>), and native code reads the object's count (its
--   pointer tag, or the lengths of a wide constructor's arrays) and takes
--   the arm only when the two agree. The arms of a match on an unboxed
--   value bind no fields (0).
type ConstructorArity = Int
armSection :: Arm comb -> GSection comb
type Branch = GBranch CombIx
type RBranch val = GBranch RComb val
data RecordFieldMappings
RecordFieldMappings :: FieldRef -> BiMap FieldName FieldRef -> RecordFieldMappings

-- | No field names assigned yet. The starting state for <a>emitCombs</a>
--   and friends, in the same spirit as <a>emptyRNs</a>.
emptyRecordFieldMappings :: RecordFieldMappings

-- | Note that the Ord instance for Field Refs is arbitrary and not tied to
--   the field name Ord instance.
convertFieldNamesToRefs :: (MonadState RecordFieldMappings m, Traversable f) => f FieldName -> m (f FieldRef)
emitCombs :: Var v => RefNums -> Reference -> Word64 -> SuperGroup Reference v -> State RecordFieldMappings (EnumMap Word64 Comb)
emitComb :: Var v => RefNums -> Reference -> Word64 -> RCtx v -> (Word64, SuperNormal Reference v) -> State RecordFieldMappings (EnumMap Word64 Comb)

-- | lazily replace all references to combinators with the combinators
--   themselves, tying the knot recursively when necessary.
resolveCombs :: Maybe (EnumMap Word64 (RCombs val)) -> EnumMap Word64 (GCombs val CombIx) -> EnumMap Word64 (RCombs val)

-- | If running in a sandboxed environment, replace all restricted foreign
--   functions with an error.
sanitizeCombsOfForeignFuncs :: Bool -> Set ForeignFunc -> EnumMap Word64 (EnumMap Word64 (GComb Void CombIx)) -> EnumMap Word64 (EnumMap Word64 (GComb Void CombIx))
absurdCombs :: EnumMap Word64 (EnumMap Word64 (GComb Void cix)) -> EnumMap Word64 (GCombs any cix)
emptyRNs :: RefNums
argsToLists :: Args -> [Int]
argsToArgs' :: Args -> Args'
countArgs :: Args -> Int

-- | How many slots an instruction pushes onto the frame, or Nothing where
--   the interpreter takes over from here (a capture, a sandboxing
--   failure). The one account of an instruction's effect on the frame: the
--   JIT's code generator lays frames out by it and <a>resultCount</a>
--   counts a primitive's results by it, so the two cannot disagree.
pushCount :: GInstr comb -> Maybe Int
combRef :: CombIx -> Reference
combDeps :: GComb val comb -> [Word64]
combTypes :: GComb any comb -> [Word64]
prettyCombs :: Word64 -> EnumMap Word64 Comb -> ShowS
prettyComb :: (Show val, Show comb) => Word64 -> Word64 -> GComb val comb -> ShowS
prettySection :: Show comb => Int -> GSection comb -> ShowS
prettyIns :: Show comb => GInstr comb -> ShowS

-- | The closure holding a Haskell value: <tt>Foreign (Wrap... x)</tt> for
--   most, a <a>TextC</a> or <a>ListC</a> for a text or a list.
class BuiltinForeign f

--   closure.

-- | The tag of base's <tt>Map</tt> type and of the functions on
--   <tt>Map</tt>, <tt>Set</tt> and <tt>Multimap</tt>, which take and
--   return it (see JIT.Config.ReplacementUse): native code wins on maps
--   below a few thousand keys, the common case, the Haskell map above
--   (JIT<i>benchmarks</i>2026-10-11-replacements.md), so the family is
--   left to the JIT.

data Stack
Stack :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> {-# UNPACK #-} !MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> {-# UNPACK #-} !MutableArray (PrimState IO) Closure -> Stack
[ap] :: Stack -> !Int
[fp] :: Stack -> !Int
[sp] :: Stack -> !Int
[ustk] :: Stack -> {-# UNPACK #-} !MutableByteArray (PrimState IO)
[bstk] :: Stack -> {-# UNPACK #-} !MutableArray (PrimState IO) Closure
type XStack = (# Int#, Int#, Int#, MutableByteArray# PrimState IO, MutableArray# PrimState IO Closure #)
pattern XStack :: Int# -> Int# -> Int# -> MutableByteArray# RealWorld -> MutableArray# RealWorld Closure -> Stack
packXStack :: XStack -> Stack

apX :: Stack -> Int#
fpX :: Stack -> Int#
spX :: Stack -> Int#

bstkX :: Stack -> MutableArray# RealWorld Closure
type Off = Int
type SZ = Int
type FP = Int
type Seg = (USeg, BSeg)
type USeg = ByteArray
type BSeg = Array Closure
type SegList = [Val]

-- | A record's field values, in ascending field-name order. Slot
--   <tt>i</tt> holds the value of field <tt>i</tt> of the accompanying
--   <a>RecordShape</a>.
type RecordVals = Vector Val

-- | A record's values from a segment: slot i holds the segment's i-th
--   value (the segments are stored backwards). Every element is an
--   evaluated <a>Val</a>, since native code reads the vector's elements as
--   closures.
recordVals :: Seg -> RecordVals

-- | Converts from the efficient stack form of a segment to the list
--   representation. Segments are stored backwards, so this reverses the
--   contents
segToList :: Seg -> SegList

-- | A runtime value, which is either a boxed or unboxed value, but we may
--   not know which.
--   
--   When it represents a boxed value, <a>getUnboxedVal</a> is meaningless,
--   but when it represents an unboxed value, <a>getBoxedVal</a> tells us
--   its type.
data Val
Val :: !UVal -> !BVal -> Val
[getUnboxedVal] :: Val -> !UVal
[getBoxedVal] :: Val -> !BVal
pattern CharVal :: Char -> Val
pattern NatVal :: Word64 -> Val
pattern DoubleVal :: Double -> Val
pattern IntVal :: Int -> Val
pattern BoolVal :: Bool -> Val
pattern UnboxedVal :: Int -> UnboxedTypeTag -> Val

-- | Matches a Val which is known to be boxed, and returns the closure
--   portion.
pattern BoxedVal :: Closure -> Val

-- | A nulled out value you can use when filling empty arrays, etc.
emptyVal :: Val
falseVal :: Val
trueVal :: Val

-- | Lift a boxed val into an Val
boxedVal :: BVal -> Val

-- | Implementation for Unison sequences. | The runtime's lists. A strict
--   deque: no thunks inside, so its structure can be read without
--   evaluating anything.
type USeq = Deque Val
traceK :: Reference -> K -> [(Reference, Int)]
frameDataSize :: K -> Int
data RuntimePanic
Panic :: String -> Maybe Val -> RuntimePanic

bnull :: BSeg

--   constructor of a data type that's been unpacked onto the stack, or
--   some tag we're about to branch on.

pokeOffS :: Stack -> Int -> USeq -> IO ()

alloc :: Int -> IO Stack

-- | The slots a fresh stack has. The JIT's <tt>ustack</tt> stress mode
--   starts with a tiny stack instead, so that growing it is exercised
--   constantly.
defaultStackSlots :: Int

-- | The code the interpreter runs: MCode over resolved combinators and
--   these values. (Defined here, below the JIT modules, so that the JIT
--   handle can be a field of the code cache without an import cycle.)
type MCombs = RCombs Val
type MSection = RSection Val
type MBranch = RBranch Val
type MInstr = RInstr Val
type MComb = RComb Val
type MRef = RRef Val

-- | Words past the last slot of the unboxed stack that native code's entry
--   point writes its results to: <tt>ap</tt>, <tt>fp</tt>, <tt>sp</tt>, a
--   count of frame records, and up to eight records of three words. Must
--   match UNISON_JIT_OUT_WORDS in jit_rt.h.
nativeOutWords :: Int

-- | Pointers past the last slot of the boxed stack, where native code
--   hands heap pointers back so that the collector sees them: the handler
--   environment it was running with when it returned, then one environment
--   per <tt>Local</tt> frame record it wrote (see <tt>pushRecord</tt> in
--   Machine.hs). Must match UNISON_JIT_OUT_PTRS in jit_rt.h.
nativeOutPtrs :: Int

-- | The slots of a boxed stack: its size less the out-area.
bstkSlots :: MutableArray RealWorld Closure -> Int
peek :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> IO Val
upeek :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> IO UVal
bpeek :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> IO BVal
peekOff :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Off -> IO Val
upeekOff :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Off -> IO UVal
bpeekOff :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Off -> IO BVal

-- | Store a boxed value. We don't bother nulling out the unboxed stack,
--   it's extra work and there's nothing to garbage collect.
bpoke :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> BVal -> IO ()
bpokeOff :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Off -> BVal -> IO ()
pokeOff :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Off -> Val -> IO ()
upokeT :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> UVal -> BVal -> IO ()
upokeOffT :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Off -> UVal -> BVal -> IO ()

-- | Sometimes we get back an int from a foreign call which we want to use
--   as a Nat. If we know it's positive and smaller than 2^63 then we can
--   safely store the Int directly as a Nat without checks.
unsafePokeIasN :: DebugCallStack => Stack -> Int -> IO ()
bump :: Stack -> IO Stack
bumpn :: Stack -> SZ -> IO Stack

-- | Eats up arguments

truncateSeg :: Stack -> SZ -> IO Stack
ensure :: Stack -> SZ -> IO Stack

-- | Like <a>ensure</a>, but grows by at least the stack's current size.
--   Native code pays for every growth by unwinding all its frames to the
--   interpreter, so it asks for room in big steps.
ensureGenerously :: Stack -> SZ -> IO Stack

-- | Converts a list of integers representing an unboxed segment back into

-- | The interpreter's side of the boundary with native code: the C
--   functions in cbits/jit_rt.c that the Haskell runtime calls, and
--   nothing else. See
--   unison-runtime<i>src</i>Unison<i>Runtime</i>JIT/design.md, "How the
--   interpreter interacts with native code". With the JIT off nothing here
--   is reached, because no cell ever holds code.
--   
--   Three jobs, in three sections below:
--   
--   <ol>
--   <li><i>Entering native code.</i> <a>enterNative</a> is the one call
--   the trampoline (Machine.runNative) makes per entry; it hands over the
--   stacks and the pool and gets a status back. Everything else native
--   code returns is read afterwards out of the stacks' out-areas with
--   <a>outAp</a> and the rest, as <a>FrameRecord</a>s for the frames of
--   native callers.</li>
--   <li><i>Startup.</i> <a>configureNative</a> passes the stress settings
--   down, <a>ctxLayout</a> and <a>rtsFacts</a> fetch the numbers the code
--   generator bakes into every function (the offsets of the C <tt>Ctx</tt>
--   struct, the RTS's info pointers and layout constants).</li>
--   <li><i>Addresses.</i> The names generated code and the IR helpers
--   call, with their addresses, which the JIT defines as absolute symbols
--   before any module is added (<a>helperAddresses</a>,
--   <a>tableAddresses</a>), and the C copies of the two helpers whose IR
--   definition must shadow them.</li>
--   </ol>
--   
--   The startup checks that run each C helper family against the
--   interpreter are in <a>Unison.Runtime.JIT.Native.Probes</a>.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Native

-- | The uniform signature of compiled code: <tt>(ctx, ap, fp, sp) -&gt;
--   status</tt>.
data NativeFn
type Status = Int
statusOK :: Status
statusError :: Status

-- | Runs native code with the given stacks (and their size in slots) and
--   pointers, and returns its status. Where it stopped and the frame
--   records it wrote are read with <a>outAp</a> and the rest. The handler
--   environment (an <tt>HEnv</tt>, coerced) goes in and comes back in the
--   boxed stack's out-area (see <a>nativeOutPtrs</a>), so that the
--   collector keeps the pointer right while Haskell code runs around the
--   call.
enterNative :: FunPtr NativeFn -> MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> MutableArray (PrimState IO) Closure -> MutableArray (PrimState IO) Closure -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> IO Status

-- | What a native caller writes down when its callee exits: which
--   <tt>Let</tt> body to continue with (an index into the frame table),
--   and the two sizes a <tt>Push</tt> frame needs. A negative index,
--   <tt>-1 - i</tt>, is a <tt>Local</tt> frame instead: the environment to
--   switch back to is in the boxed out-area at <tt>i</tt> past the first
--   pointer, and the pending-argument count is as for a <tt>Push</tt>.
data FrameRecord
FrameRecord :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> FrameRecord
[frIndex] :: FrameRecord -> !Int
[frFrameSize] :: FrameRecord -> !Int
[frPendingArgs] :: FrameRecord -> !Int
outAp :: MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> Int -> IO Int
outFp :: MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> Int -> IO Int
outSp :: MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> Int -> IO Int
outFrameCount :: MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> Int -> IO Int

-- | The frame records, in the order they were written (innermost caller
--   first). Call at most once per entry: a long list is freed as it is
--   read.
outFrames :: MutableByteArray (PrimState IO) -> Int -> IO [FrameRecord]

-- | Passes stress settings to the C side: poll every N entries, treat
--   every Nth callee as uncompiled, C stack budget in bytes (0 for the
--   default), allocation budget in words, trace. Called once at startup.
configureNative :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Bool -> IO ()

-- | The offsets of the fields of the C <tt>Ctx</tt>, in the order they are
--   declared, and its total size. The code generator uses these.
ctxLayout :: IO ([Int], Int)

-- | Facts about the runtime that generated code needs: see
--   unison_jit_rts_facts in jit_rt.c for what each entry is.
rtsFacts :: IO [Int]

-- | For tracing: what the poll would see right now.
hplimValue :: IO Int

-- | Every C function generated code and the IR modules call by name, with
--   its address, for the JIT to define before any module is added (so that
--   nothing is looked up in the process, which Linux and Windows don't
--   allow without more linker flags).
helperAddresses :: IO [(String, Word64)]

-- | The names the IR helpers refer to the runtime's tables by, with the
--   tables' addresses, for the JIT to define before the helpers are added.
tableAddresses :: IO [(String, Word64)]

-- | Where the C copy of <tt>unison_jit_murmur</tt> is: what the JIT's own
--   definition of the name (the IR copy) must not be.
murmurCAddress :: FunPtr (Int64 -> Ptr () -> IO ())

-- | Where the C copy of <tt>unison_jit_ucmp</tt> is, for the same check.
ucmpCAddress :: FunPtr (Int64 -> Ptr () -> Int64 -> Ptr () -> Int64 -> IO ())
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Unison.Runtime.JIT.Native.FrameRecord


-- | Turning a Unison function into a C-callable function pointer, so that
--   C code can call back into Unison. This is the mirror image of the
--   dynamic call in <a>Unison.Runtime.Machine</a>: there, Unison stack
--   values are marshalled into a libffi argument buffer and a C function
--   is called; here a C caller fills an argument buffer, a libffi
--   <i>closure</i> invokes a single generic Haskell entry point, we decode
--   the arguments directly onto a Unison stack, run the Unison function,
--   and marshal its result (left on the stack) back into the C return
--   slot.
--   
--   The Haskell <tt>libffi</tt> package does not expose the closure API,
--   so the three <tt>ffi_closure_*</tt> entry points are imported directly
--   (they are linked via that package already), as is done for
--   <tt>ffi_prep_cif_var</tt> in <a>Unison.Runtime.Foreign.Dynamic</a>.
--   
--   Running the Unison function is supplied by the caller (a <tt>Stack
--   -&gt; (Stack -&gt; IO ()) -&gt; IO ()</tt> action, in practice a
--   partially-applied evaluator entry) so that this module does not depend
--   on the evaluator. Arguments are written straight to the stack rather
--   than through an intermediate <tt>[Val]</tt>, so the marshalling
--   allocates nothing beyond the stack itself.
module Unison.Runtime.Foreign.Callback

-- | Runs the Unison function from a callback: the given stack already
--   holds the decoded C arguments (pushed in parameter order); apply the
--   function to them and hand the result stack to the continuation (the
--   result on top). Supplied by the evaluator so this module stays off it.
--   Expected to be synchronous.
type RunCallback = Stack -> Stack -> IO () -> IO ()

-- | Build a C-callable function pointer from a Unison function. The
--   <a>FFSpec</a> describes the C signature; <tt>run</tt> applies the
--   Unison function to the arguments the callback decodes onto the stack.
--   The result is a <a>CDynFunc</a> (so it flows through the same paths as
--   a symbol loaded from a DLL) whose underlying pointer calls back into
--   Unison.
--   
--   The returned callback holds the Unison function (and anything it
--   closes over) alive until <a>freeCallback</a> is called; using the
--   pointer afterwards is a use-after-free, exactly as with a freed
--   <a>Dynamic</a> pointer.
mkCallback :: FFSpec -> RunCallback -> IO CDynFunc

-- | Release a callback created by <a>mkCallback</a>: frees the libffi
--   closure and drops the reference keeping the Unison function alive.
--   Safe to call more than once, and a no-op on a <a>CDynFunc</a> that is
--   not a callback (e.g. a DLL symbol, whose finalizer is <tt>pure
--   ()</tt>).
freeCallback :: CDynFunc -> IO ()
data CallbackException

-- | A callback argument/result type that is not supported.
UnsupportedCallbackType :: FFType -> CallbackException

-- | <tt>ffi_prep_closure_loc</tt> failed.
BadClosureInit :: CallbackException
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Unison.Runtime.Foreign.Callback.CallbackException
instance GHC.Internal.Exception.Type.Exception Unison.Runtime.Foreign.Callback.CallbackException
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Unison.Runtime.Foreign.Callback.CallbackException

module Unison.Runtime.Exception
data RuntimeExn

-- | pretty exception
PE :: CallStack -> [Word] -> Pretty ColorText -> RuntimeExn

-- | a failure in Unison code
BU :: [(Reference, Int)] -> Text -> Val -> RuntimeExn
die :: HasCallStack => [Word] -> String -> IO a
exn :: HasCallStack => [Word] -> String -> a
instance GHC.Internal.Exception.Type.Exception Unison.Runtime.Exception.RuntimeExn
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Unison.Runtime.Exception.RuntimeExn

-- | The frame table, one per JIT. A native caller whose callee exits
--   writes a frame record naming an entry here; the trampoline turns the
--   record into the <tt>Push</tt> frame the interpreter would have pushed.
--   See unison-runtime<i>src</i>Unison<i>Runtime</i>JIT/design.md,
--   "Frames: native code records, Haskell builds".
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Frames

-- | The fixed parts of a <tt>Push</tt> frame for one <tt>Let</tt>: the
--   body's <tt>CombIx</tt>, stack guard and section, and the cell holding
--   the body's native code.
data Frame
Frame :: !CombIx -> !Int -> !MSection -> !Ptr NativeCell -> Frame

-- | 1-based.
type FrameIndex = Int
data Frames
newFrames :: IO Frames

-- | Adds a module's frames and returns the index of the first one. The
--   rest follow consecutively, in the order given.
registerFrames :: Frames -> [Frame] -> IO FrameIndex

-- | Overwrites frames registered earlier, starting at the given index (see
--   replaceExits).
replaceFrames :: Frames -> FrameIndex -> [Frame] -> IO ()
lookupFrame :: Frames -> FrameIndex -> IO Frame


-- | The exits table, one per JIT (which is one per process, see JIT.hs).
--   Native code returns an index into it to say what the interpreter
--   should do next. See
--   unison-runtime<i>src</i>Unison<i>Runtime</i>JIT/design.md.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Exits
data Exit

-- | interpret from this section of this combinator
Resume :: !CombIx -> !MSection -> Exit

-- | grow the Unison stack to fit a frame of this size, then call the
--   function whose cell this is again (it may not be the one the
--   trampoline entered: tail calls change functions)
GrowStack :: !Int -> !Ptr NativeCell -> Exit

-- | the runtime asked the thread to stop; call the function whose cell
--   this is again when the thread next runs
Reenter :: !Ptr NativeCell -> Exit

-- | run this instruction with the interpreter (it pushes the given number
--   of values), then call the function in this cell, which continues with
--   the section after it. If the instruction pushed a different number of
--   values, interpret that section instead.
CallOut :: !CombIx -> !MInstr -> !MSection -> !Int -> !Ptr NativeCell -> Exit

-- | a description, for statistics
Named :: String -> Exit -> Exit

-- | An exit the code didn't cause: the poll (the context-switch flag or
--   the allocation budget) and stack growth land wherever the program
--   happens to be. The others, a call-out or a resume, are taken at a
--   point the code itself reaches on every such path.
isAdHoc :: Exit -> Bool

-- | 1-based; 0 is OK and negative values are errors.
type ExitIndex = Int

-- | The table, the exit counters, and the entry counts (by code address)
--   with the names of the functions entered.
data Exits

-- | An empty table. With statistics on, the counters have a slot per exit
--   index (up to <a>counterSlots</a>); otherwise one, since nothing
--   counts.
newExits :: Bool -> IO Exits

-- | Adds a module's exits and returns the index of the first one. The rest
--   follow consecutively, in the order given.
registerExits :: Exits -> [Exit] -> IO ExitIndex

-- | Overwrites exits registered earlier, starting at the given index: the
--   second code generation pass produces the final ones (with the cells of
--   the auxiliary functions), the first only their number.
replaceExits :: Exits -> ExitIndex -> [Exit] -> IO ()
lookupExit :: Exits -> ExitIndex -> IO Exit

-- | Counts an exit; gives the total taken so far.
countExit :: Exits -> ExitIndex -> IO Int

-- | Every exit that has been taken, with its count.
exitCounts :: Exits -> IO [(ExitIndex, Exit, Int)]

-- | Starts counting again from zero.
resetExitCounts :: Exits -> IO ()

-- | For <tt>UNISON_JIT_STATS</tt>: how often the trampoline entered each
--   native function (by code address), and what each is called. Slow (a
--   map in an IORef); statistics runs only.
countEntry :: Exits -> Ptr a -> IO ()

-- | Records the name of the function at a code address.
nameEntry :: Exits -> Ptr a -> String -> IO ()

-- | The entries counted since the last call, by function name.
entryCounts :: Exits -> IO [(String, Int)]


-- | The constant pool: Haskell heap objects that native code needs, in an
--   array whose address is passed on every entry. See
--   unison-runtime<i>src</i>Unison<i>Runtime</i>JIT/design.md, "Appendix:
--   the constant pool", which also says why there is one pool per process
--   rather than one per module.
--   
--   Indices are assigned when a module is compiled (<a>poolIndices</a>)
--   and are constants in the generated code. The array grows by copying;
--   the old arrays are kept, and new entries are written to them too where
--   they fit, so an address read at entry stays valid for as long as that
--   native run lasts. A run can still meet code that was installed after
--   it began and uses an index past the end of the array the run holds: a
--   function that uses an index of <a>poolStableSize</a> or more checks
--   the array's size at entry, and exits to be entered again with the
--   current array.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Pool

-- | The size of the first array: every array ever passed to native code
--   has at least this many entries. | A pool, with the size its first
--   array has: a function that uses only indices below it never has to
--   check the array it was given (the stress mode <tt>pool=N</tt> makes it
--   tiny, so that growing is exercised).
data Pool

-- | A pool holding the fixed entries. The argument is the stress mode's
--   size for the first array, if any.
newPool :: Maybe Int -> IO Pool

-- | What a pool entry is. Entries are interned by key.
data PoolKey

-- | a constructor with no fields. Also how a <a>Reference</a> is kept: the
--   entry for <tt>KeyEnum r 0</tt> is an <a>Enum</a> whose reference field
--   native code reads when it builds a constructor of that type.
KeyEnum :: !Reference -> !PackedTag -> PoolKey

-- | a boxed literal (text, term link, type link)
KeyLit :: !MLit -> PoolKey

-- | a known combinator as a value: a <tt>PAp</tt> with nothing captured,
--   the same closure the interpreter builds for <tt>App (Env cix)
--   ZArgs</tt>. Interned by the CombIx alone (the combinator has no Ord).
KeyComb :: !CombIx -> !GCombInfo MComb -> PoolKey

-- | the boxed part of a top-level value that was evaluated when its
--   definition was loaded (a <tt>CachedVal</tt>), by its CombIx
KeyCached :: !CombIx -> !Closure -> PoolKey

-- | a record shape, kept as an empty record of that shape: native code
--   copies the shape's words out of it when it builds a record
--   (<tt>RecPack</tt>). Interned by the field names, which determine the
--   shape.
KeyRecord :: !RecordShape -> PoolKey

-- | The index of each key, adding the ones not seen before. Called when a
--   module is compiled, before its code is generated.
poolIndices :: Pool -> [PoolKey] -> IO (Map PoolKey Int)

-- | The array to pass to native code now.
currentPool :: Pool -> IO (MutableArray (PrimState IO) Closure)
poolStableSize :: Pool -> Int
poolIndexCharTag :: Int
poolIndexFloatTag :: Int
poolIndexIntTag :: Int
poolIndexNatTag :: Int

-- | The boolean closures, for comparison results.
poolIndexTrue :: Int

-- | The boolean closures, for comparison results.
poolIndexFalse :: Int
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Unison.Runtime.JIT.Pool.PoolKey
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Unison.Runtime.JIT.Pool.PoolKey
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Unison.Runtime.JIT.Pool.PoolKey

module Unison.Runtime
type Runtime = Runtime Error DecompError
pattern Runtime :: forall {e} {e'} {v}. IO () -> (CodeLookup v IO () -> PrettyPrintEnv -> ProfileSpec -> Term v -> IO (Either e (Response e', Term v))) -> (CompileOpts -> CodeLookup v IO () -> PrettyPrintEnv -> Reference -> FilePath -> IO (Maybe e)) -> Type v Ann -> NESet (Type v Ann) -> Runtime e e' v
terminate :: Runtime e e' v -> IO ()
evaluate :: Runtime e e' v -> CodeLookup v IO () -> PrettyPrintEnv -> ProfileSpec -> Term v -> IO (Either e (Response e', Term v))
compileTo :: Runtime e e' v -> CompileOpts -> CodeLookup v IO () -> PrettyPrintEnv -> Reference -> FilePath -> IO (Maybe e)
mainType :: Runtime e e' v -> Type v Ann
ioTestTypes :: Runtime e e' v -> NESet (Type v Ann)
data Error

--   few places that have unstructured errors.

RuntimeExn :: Maybe (PrettyPrintEnv, Reference -> Reference, Val -> DecompResult Symbol) -> RuntimeExn -> Error
RuntimePanic :: PrettyPrintEnv -> (Val -> DecompResult Symbol) -> RuntimePanic -> Error

-- | Serializes a <a>SuperGroup</a> for rehashing.
--   
--   Expected as arguments are some code, and the <a>Reference</a> that
--   refers to it. In particular, if the code refers to itself by
--   reference, or if the code is part of a mututally-recursive set of
--   definitions (which have a common hash), the reference used as part of
--   that (mutual) recursion must be supplied.
--   
--   Using that reference, we find all references in the code to that
--   connected component. In the resulting byte string, those references
--   are instead replaced by positions in a listing of the connected
--   component. This means that the byte string is independent of the hash
--   used for the self reference. Only the order matters (which is
--   determined by the <a>Reference</a>). Then the bytes can be re-hashed
--   to establish a new hash for the connected component. This operation
--   should be idempotent as long as the indexing is preserved.
--   
--   Supplying a <a>Builtin</a> reference is not supported. Such code
--   shouldn't be subject to rehashing.
serializeGroupForRehash :: Var v => Reference -> SuperGroup Reference v -> ByteString
getVersionedValue :: forall (m :: Type -> Type). PrimBase m => Get m (Referenced Value)
deserializeValue :: ByteString -> IO (Either String (Referenced Value))
serializeValue :: Referenced Value -> ByteString
serializeValueWithVersion :: Word64 -> Referenced Value -> IO ByteString
serializeValueForHash :: Value Reference -> ByteString
getGroupCurrent :: forall (m :: Type -> Type) v. (PrimBase m, Var v) => Get m (SuperGroup Reference v)
type GDeserial (m :: Type -> Type) a = (Version, Bool) -> Get m a
type DeserialIO a = (Version, Bool) -> Get IO a
type DeserialST s a = (Version, Bool) -> Get ST s a
valueToCode :: Version -> Version
valueVersion :: Word32
codeVersion :: Word32
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Unison.Runtime.ANF.Serialize.Version
