-- | Closure layouts, found by probing sample closures at startup (see
--   design.md, <a>Layouts</a>). Generated code uses these as constants. If
--   a layout isn't what the code generator expects, the JIT is turned off.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Layout
data Layout
Layout :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> (Int -> Int) -> Layout

-- | info pointer, to write into new closures of this kind
[lInfo] :: Layout -> !Int

-- | the low bits of a pointer to this constructor
[lPtrTag] :: Layout -> !Int

-- | pointer fields come first in the payload; this is how many
[lPtrs] :: Layout -> !Int
[lNptrs] :: Layout -> !Int

-- | byte offset from the untagged closure address to payload word i
[lFieldOffset] :: Layout -> Int -> Int
data Layouts
Layouts :: !Vector Layout -> !Pair Int Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Layout -> !Layout -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Pair Int Int -> !Layout -> !Layout -> !Int -> Layouts

-- | the data constructors with 0 to 6 fields, by field count: <tt>DataN
--   tag (Val u b)... ref</tt>, with the fields' boxed halves as pointers 0
--   to n-1, the reference as pointer n, the tag as the first non-pointer
--   word and the fields' unboxed halves after it. Pointer tags 3 to 5 for
--   0 to 2 fields and 6 for 5 fields (base's Map node); 3, 4 and 6 fields
--   share tag 7 with the rest.
[lData] :: Layouts -> !Vector Layout

-- | <tt>TextC rope</tt>, <tt>ListC deque</tt> and <tt>BytesC rope</tt> as
--   (info pointer, pointer tag): one pointer each, the rope (Text is a
--   newtype over it) or the deque; tags 1 and 2 for texts and lists, 7 for
--   bytes
[lText] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | <tt>TextC rope</tt>, <tt>ListC deque</tt> and <tt>BytesC rope</tt> as
--   (info pointer, pointer tag): one pointer each, the rope (Text is a
--   newtype over it) or the deque; tags 1 and 2 for texts and lists, 7 for
--   bytes
[lList] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | <tt>TextC rope</tt>, <tt>ListC deque</tt> and <tt>BytesC rope</tt> as
--   (info pointer, pointer tag): one pointer each, the rope (Text is a
--   newtype over it) or the deque; tags 1 and 2 for texts and lists, 7 for
--   bytes
[lBytes] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | <tt>DataG tag useg bseg ref</tt> (seven or more fields): pointers the
--   ByteArray#, the Array# and the reference; one non-pointer, the tag;
--   pointer tag 7
[lDataG] :: Layouts -> !Layout

-- | <tt>PAp (CIx ref grp w) (LamI arity fsize entry cell) useg bseg</tt>,
--   with CombIx and GCombInfo unpacked: pointers ref, entry, the
--   ByteArray#, the Array#; non-pointers grp, w, arity, fsize, cell;
--   pointer tag 7
[lPAp] :: Layouts -> !Layout

-- | <tt>Foreign x</tt>: pointer tag 7, one pointer, the Foreign
[lForeignInfo] :: Layouts -> !Int

-- | <tt>WrapIORef ref</tt>: pointer tag 7, one pointer, the MutVar#
[lIORefInfo] :: Layouts -> !Int

-- | <tt>WrapMutableArray arr</tt>: pointer tag 7, one pointer, the
--   MutableArray#
[lMutableArrayInfo] :: Layouts -> !Int

-- | the other wrappers the array and ref builtins see, as (info pointer,
--   pointer tag): <tt>WrapArray</tt>, <tt>WrapMutableByteArray</tt>,
--   <tt>WrapByteArray</tt> (one pointer each, the unlifted array),
--   <tt>WrapTicket</tt> (one pointer, the ticket's value) and
--   <tt>WrapPtr</tt> (one non-pointer, the address)
[lArrayWrap] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | the other wrappers the array and ref builtins see, as (info pointer,
--   pointer tag): <tt>WrapArray</tt>, <tt>WrapMutableByteArray</tt>,
--   <tt>WrapByteArray</tt> (one pointer each, the unlifted array),
--   <tt>WrapTicket</tt> (one pointer, the ticket's value) and
--   <tt>WrapPtr</tt> (one non-pointer, the address)
[lMutableByteArrayWrap] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | the other wrappers the array and ref builtins see, as (info pointer,
--   pointer tag): <tt>WrapArray</tt>, <tt>WrapMutableByteArray</tt>,
--   <tt>WrapByteArray</tt> (one pointer each, the unlifted array),
--   <tt>WrapTicket</tt> (one pointer, the ticket's value) and
--   <tt>WrapPtr</tt> (one non-pointer, the address)
[lByteArrayWrap] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | the other wrappers the array and ref builtins see, as (info pointer,
--   pointer tag): <tt>WrapArray</tt>, <tt>WrapMutableByteArray</tt>,
--   <tt>WrapByteArray</tt> (one pointer each, the unlifted array),
--   <tt>WrapTicket</tt> (one pointer, the ticket's value) and
--   <tt>WrapPtr</tt> (one non-pointer, the address)
[lTicketWrap] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | the other wrappers the array and ref builtins see, as (info pointer,
--   pointer tag): <tt>WrapArray</tt>, <tt>WrapMutableByteArray</tt>,
--   <tt>WrapByteArray</tt> (one pointer each, the unlifted array),
--   <tt>WrapTicket</tt> (one pointer, the ticket's value) and
--   <tt>WrapPtr</tt> (one non-pointer, the address)
[lPtrWrap] :: Layouts -> !Pair Int Int

-- | <tt>Val u b</tt>: pointer tag 1; pointer b, then non-pointer u
[lVal] :: Layouts -> !Layout

-- | <tt>RecordG shape vals</tt> with the shape and the vector unpacked:
--   pointer tag 7; pointers the field names' Array#, the field numbers'
--   and the slots' ByteArray#s and the values' Array#; non-pointers the
--   shape reference, the names' offset and length, the values' offset and
--   length ("records" in jit_internal.h)
[lRecord] :: Layouts -> !Layout

-- | header size in bytes; payload starts after it
[lHeaderBytes] :: Layouts -> !Int

-- | Probes the layouts the code generator relies on. Returns an
--   explanation if anything is unexpected.
probeLayouts :: IO (Either String Layouts)

-- | Lists: teaches the C helpers (jit_rt.c) the constructors of
--   Unison.Util.Deque from samples, checks the structure of a range of
--   lists against what the helpers assume, and then runs every helper
--   against the Haskell operation it stands in for; each list a helper
--   builds is checked for its structure too. Returns an explanation if
--   anything differs.
--   
--   <tt>steps</tt> (stress mode <tt>lists=N</tt>) adds a longer test: that
--   many random operations, each done by a helper on the results of
--   earlier ones and compared with the Haskell operation.
probeLists :: Layouts -> Int -> IO (Either String ())

-- | Text: the same for the text helpers. Each helper is run against the
--   Haskell operation on texts of many shapes (one chunk, deep ropes,
--   several bytes per character), and every text a helper builds is
--   checked for its structure too.
--   
--   <tt>steps</tt> (stress mode <tt>texts=N</tt>) adds the longer test, as
--   for lists: that many random operations, each done by a helper on the
--   results of earlier ones and compared with the Haskell operation.
probeTexts :: Layouts -> Int -> IO (Either String ())

-- | The bytes helpers: the same arrangement as <a>probeTexts</a> for
--   <tt>Bytes</tt>, which is the same rope with chunks of bytes, plus
--   <tt>Bytes.at</tt> and <tt>Bytes.flatten</tt>. Stress mode
--   <tt>bytes=N</tt>.
probeBytes :: Layouts -> Int -> IO (Either String ())

-- | Partial applications: the helper for the <tt>Name</tt> instruction
--   against what the interpreter builds, for closures with and without
--   arguments already captured.
probeNames :: Layouts -> IO (Either String ())

-- | Teaches the C array and ref helpers the wrappers' info pointers and
--   tags, and the runtime's empty value (what <tt>Scope.array</tt> fills
--   with).
probeArrays :: Layouts -> IO (Either String ())

-- | Teaches the hash helper the closures it needs to recognize and checks
--   it against the Haskell hash (reflection then
--   <a>hash64ValueUntyped</a>) on sample values of every kind it handles.
probeMurmur :: Layouts -> IO (Either String ())

-- | Universal equality and ordering: hands the comparison helpers what
--   they need beyond the other tables (see unison_jit_cmp_init), then runs
--   pairs of every kind of value through the C copies and the
--   interpreter's <tt>Eq Val</tt> and <tt>Ord Val</tt>; any difference, or
--   a pair the helper should handle and doesn't, turns the JIT off.
probeCompare :: Layouts -> IO (Either String ())

-- | The handler environment: teaches the request helpers the layouts of
--   <tt>HEnv</tt>, the <tt>IntMap</tt> under <tt>EnumMap</tt>, the
--   <tt>STRef</tt> box inside an <tt>AffineRef</tt> and the
--   <tt>Affine</tt> closure, from samples, and checks the native lookup
--   against what the interpreter's <tt>resolve</tt> would find (see
--   unison_jit_env_init in jit_rt.c).
probeEnv :: IO (Either String ())

-- | Records: hands the record helpers sample records (see
--   unison_jit_record_init), which checks the layout and the field lookup
--   against them, then runs records through the hash and the comparison
--   helpers against the Haskell answers.
probeRecords :: Layouts -> IO (Either String ())


-- | MCode to LLVM IR, for the subset the JIT supports. See design.md for
--   the conventions ("Code generation" for how this module is organized).
--   
--   Within a function, every Unison stack slot is an LLVM alloca:
--   <tt>%u<a>k</a></tt> holds the unboxed word and <tt>%b<a>k</a></tt> the
--   boxed pointer of the slot at frame offset <tt>k</tt>, which is stack
--   index <tt>fp + k</tt>. The frame depth <tt>d</tt> (the interpreter's
--   <tt>sp - fp</tt>) is known statically at every point, so MCode's "slot
--   <tt>i</tt> from the top" is frame offset <tt>d - i</tt>. The real
--   stack is touched only at entry, before a tail call, and on exit paths.
--   
--   The generator is strict throughout (see
--   <a>Unison.Runtime.JIT.Strict</a>): its text is <a>Text</a>, its
--   sequences are <a>Deque</a>s, its pairs are <a>Pair</a>s, and every
--   field of its state is strict, so nothing it builds is a thunk.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Codegen
data Env
Env :: !Layouts -> !CtxOffsets -> !Int -> !Int -> !Bool -> !Bool -> !Bool -> !MCombs -> !Map PoolKey Int -> !RtsFacts -> !Map Reference Word64 -> !Cells -> !Deque Text -> !Bool -> !AuxMemo -> !Map (Ptr NativeCell) Text -> !Map (Ptr NativeCell) (Pair Text Int) -> !Bool -> !Bool -> !Switches -> !Int -> Env
[envLayouts] :: Env -> !Layouts
[envCtx] :: Env -> !CtxOffsets

-- | index of this module's first exit in the global table
[envExitBase] :: Env -> !Int

-- | index of this module's first frame in the global frame table
[envFrameBase] :: Env -> !Int

-- | emit the stress-mode poll countdown
[envStressPoll] :: Env -> !Bool

-- | emit the stress-mode "callee not compiled" countdown
[envStressCallee] :: Env -> !Bool

-- | exits write the frame back through a call (see <a>joinCall</a>)
[envExitCall] :: Env -> !Bool

-- | the group being compiled, for the arity of Let body combinators
[envCombs] :: Env -> !MCombs

-- | pool index of every constant this group uses
[envPool] :: Env -> !Map PoolKey Int
[envRts] :: Env -> !RtsFacts

-- | the number each type reference has in the cache (the type part of a
--   packed tag), for the one match arm that compares a whole tag (a lone
--   wide constructor's; no other declaration of a type is needed: field
--   counts come from the arms and the objects, <a>genDMatchClosure</a>)
[envTypeNumbers] :: Env -> !Map Reference Word64

-- | cells for the auxiliary functions (re-entry points), taken in order
[envCells] :: Env -> !Cells

-- | features turned off for debugging (see Config)
[envDisabled] :: Env -> !Deque Text

-- | leave the re-entry points that are only used when something exits
--   (bodies of Lets inside bindings, slow paths of instructions with a
--   native fast path) to be generated when they turn out to be used: each
--   gets a cell and a <a>Deferred</a>, but no code
[envLazy] :: Env -> !Bool

-- | the auxiliary functions already known for the function this one
--   belongs to, generated or deferred: a re-entry function generated later
--   reuses the cells its parent handed out
[envKnown] :: Env -> !AuxMemo

-- | the functions defined in the module being generated, by cell: a call
--   to one of them is a direct call to its symbol, which LLVM can inline,
--   instead of a call through the cell
[envLocal] :: Env -> !Map (Ptr NativeCell) Text

-- | the functions of this module that have a worker (see <a>feWorker</a>),
--   by cell: the worker's symbol and its arity
[envWorkers] :: Env -> !Map (Ptr NativeCell) (Pair Text Int)

-- | the code is from a sandboxed code cache: Ref.cas and Ref.readForCas
--   are left to the interpreter, which refuses them
[envSandboxed] :: Env -> !Bool

-- | the function's own symbol gets internal linkage: it is a private copy
--   of a callee (see Compile's <tt>uCopy</tt>), which LLVM drops once it
--   is inlined at every call. Its worker is internal already; its
--   auxiliary functions stay external, since they are installed in cells
[envInternal] :: Env -> !Bool

-- | what the settings turn on in the generator (see <a>switches</a>)
[envSwitches] :: Env -> !Switches

-- | the size of the constant pool's first array (see Pool): a function
--   that uses only indices below it never checks the array it was given
[envPoolStable] :: Env -> !Int

-- | The cells left for auxiliary functions: a supply without end (the
--   first pass over a module, which only counts what each function needs),
--   or what remains of the module's block.
data Cells
Counting :: Cells
Cells :: !Deque (Ptr NativeCell) -> Cells

-- | Byte offsets of the fields of the C <tt>Ctx</tt>, from
--   <tt>unison_jit_ctx_layout</tt>.
data CtxOffsets
CtxOffsets :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> CtxOffsets
[oUstk] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oBstk] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oPool] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oStackSize] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oHplim] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oAp] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oFp] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oSp] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oMaxSp] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oStressPoll] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oStressPollLeft] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oStressCallee] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oStressCalleeLeft] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oFrames] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oNFrames] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oMaxFrames] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oCStackLimit] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oCap] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oBudgetEnd] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oHp] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oHpLim] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oHenv] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int
[oNLocals] :: CtxOffsets -> !Int

-- | From unison_jit_rts_facts: the info pointers and layouts of the two
--   arrays a <tt>Seg</tt> is made of.
data RtsFacts
RtsFacts :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> RtsFacts
[rArrWordsInfo] :: RtsFacts -> !Int
[rArrPtrsInfo] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | ByteArray#: header words including the byte count, and the word index
--   of the count
[rBytesHeader] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | ByteArray#: header words including the byte count, and the word index
--   of the count
[rBytesCount] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | Array#: header words, word index of the element count and of the
--   payload size
[rPtrsHeader] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | Array#: header words, word index of the element count and of the
--   payload size
[rPtrsCount] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | Array#: header words, word index of the element count and of the
--   payload size
[rPtrsSize] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | log2 of elements per card-table byte
[rCardBits] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | word index of a MutVar#'s content
[rMutVarVar] :: RtsFacts -> !Int

-- | info pointer a mutable Array# gets when written
[rArrPtrsDirtyInfo] :: RtsFacts -> !Int
data Function
Function :: !Text -> !Text -> !Deque Exit -> !Deque Frame -> !Ptr NativeCell -> !Deque (Pair Text (Ptr NativeCell)) -> !Deque Deferred -> !AuxMemo -> !Deque Text -> Function
[fnName] :: Function -> !Text

-- | the LLVM text of the function and what comes with it (a module's IR
--   can run to tens of megabytes)
[fnIR] :: Function -> !Text

-- | in index order, starting at the module's base plus the count before
--   this function
[fnExits] :: Function -> !Deque Exit

-- | likewise for the frame table
[fnFrames] :: Function -> !Deque Frame
[fnCell] :: Function -> !Ptr NativeCell

-- | the auxiliary functions defined alongside (re-entry points after
--   call-outs, bodies of Lets inside bindings) and their cells
[fnAux] :: Function -> !Deque (Pair Text (Ptr NativeCell))

-- | the re-entry functions given a cell but left for later
[fnDeferred] :: Function -> !Deque Deferred

-- | every auxiliary function known after this one was generated
[fnMemo] :: Function -> !AuxMemo

-- | why parts of the function fell back to the interpreter
[fnNotes] :: Function -> !Deque Text

-- | A re-entry function that was given a cell but not generated: all that
--   <a>genDeferred</a> needs to generate it later.
data Deferred
Deferred :: !Text -> !CombIx -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !MSection -> !Ptr NativeCell -> Deferred
[dName] :: Deferred -> !Text
[dCix] :: Deferred -> !CombIx

-- | slots on the stack at entry
[dLoaded] :: Deferred -> !Int
[dFrameSize] :: Deferred -> !Int

-- | the frame base (see <a>feBase</a>)
[dBase] :: Deferred -> !Int
[dBody] :: Deferred -> !MSection
[dCell] :: Deferred -> !Ptr NativeCell

-- | What an auxiliary function is generated from: the section (without its
--   combinator references, which have no Ord; their CombIx stays), the
--   depth it starts at, and the frame base.
type AuxKey = (GSection (), Int, Int)
type AuxMemo = Map AuxKey Pair Text Ptr NativeCell

-- | Compiles one combinator, or says why it can't be.
genFunction :: Env -> Text -> CombIx -> Int -> Int -> MSection -> Ptr NativeCell -> Either Text Function

-- | Generates a re-entry function that was left for later.
genDeferred :: Env -> Deferred -> Either Text Function

-- | Declarations every module needs.
modulePrelude :: Text

-- | How many slots an instruction pushes onto the frame, or Nothing where
--   the interpreter takes over from here (a capture, a sandboxing
--   failure). The one account of an instruction's effect on the frame: the
--   JIT's code generator lays frames out by it and <a>resultCount</a>
--   counts a primitive's results by it, so the two cannot disagree.
pushCount :: GInstr comb -> Maybe Int

-- | Whether a <tt>Let</tt> binding is generated inline: its first node
--   must be one the generator has code for. A binding that would exit
--   straight away is better left to the interpreter along with its
--   <tt>Let</tt>, which saves the binding's frame record. (Whether a whole
--   function is worth compiling is decided before this, in JIT.Estimate.)
startsSupported :: Switches -> MSection -> Bool

-- | Whether an instruction the generator can't compile can be a call-out
--   with native code after it.
callOutWorthwhile :: GInstr (RComb Val) -> MSection -> Bool
instrNative :: Switches -> GInstr comb -> Bool

-- | <a>instrNative</a> for an instruction in its section: an affine
--   handler's <tt>InLocal</tt> is native (a no-op) when the rest of its
--   case can't tell the environment wasn't switched, see
--   <a>localUnobserved</a>.
instrNativeIn :: Switches -> GInstr (RComb Val) -> MSection -> Bool

-- | What the settings turn on in the generator, for the predicates above,
--   which the estimator asks without a function environment in reach.
data Switches
Switches :: !Bool -> !Bool -> !Bool -> Switches

-- | ability requests and the affine handler instructions are generated
--   (off under <tt>UNISON_JIT_DISABLE=requests</tt>)
[swRequests] :: Switches -> !Bool

-- | the record instructions are generated (off under
--   <tt>UNISON_JIT_DISABLE=records</tt>)
[swRecords] :: Switches -> !Bool

-- | the observing form of <tt>InLocal</tt> is generated (see
--   <a>genInLocal</a>): its Local frame record is written by the exit
--   routine, which the generated write-back blocks of
--   <tt>UNISON_JIT_EXITS=blocks</tt> don't have
[swLocalObserving] :: Switches -> !Bool
switches :: Config -> Switches

-- | The foreign functions whose result is unit (they need the constant).
unitForeign :: [ForeignFunc]

-- | Whether a combinator can have a worker: every return it makes itself
--   yields exactly one value. (Its tail calls return whatever their
--   callees do; a caller that expects one value from this function gets
--   one.) This is a first sieve: how many values a <tt>Yield (VArgV
--   i)</tt> returns depends on the frame depth, which only generating the
--   code finds out, and generating a worker fails if it turns out not to
--   be one.
workerShape :: MSection -> Bool
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Unison.Runtime.JIT.Codegen.SharedKey
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Unison.Runtime.JIT.Codegen.SharedKey


-- | Deciding, before compiling a function, whether native code for it
--   would be faster than the interpreter. See design.md, "What isn't
--   compiled".
--   
--   What compiling saves is the interpreter's overhead (dispatch and stack
--   traffic), a few nanoseconds per instruction; the instruction's own
--   work costs the same either way. What it can cost is exits: leaving
--   native code for something only the interpreter can do, and coming
--   back, is a round trip worth several instructions' savings. So a
--   function that does one foreign call and little else is slower
--   compiled.
--   
--   The estimate walks the function's MCode and computes, for an average
--   path from entry to return, the saving (in units of one simple
--   instruction's overhead) and the number of exits that are certain:
--   taken every time the code runs. Exits that only happen on a slow path
--   (a fast path's miss, the poll, stack growth) don't count.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Estimate

-- | For an average path through a function: the interpreter overhead that
--   native code avoids, and the exits it is certain to take.
data Estimate
Estimate :: !Double -> !Double -> !Bool -> Estimate
[esSaving] :: Estimate -> !Double
[esExits] :: Estimate -> !Double

-- | the path calls the function itself: it is a loop or a recursion
[esRec] :: Estimate -> !Bool

-- | Whether the function in this cell, with this body, is worth compiling,
--   and the estimate that says so (Nothing for code that never returns).
--   The verdict is recorded in the cell. Callees that have not been judged
--   are judged on the way, and their verdicts recorded too, so the answer
--   doesn't depend on the order in which functions get hot.
judge :: Config -> Ptr NativeCell -> MSection -> IO (Bool, Maybe Estimate)


-- | Compiling a group of combinators to a native module and installing the
--   result in their cells. See design.md, "What gets compiled, and when".
module Unison.Runtime.JIT.Compile

-- | What compiling needs and what it keeps between compilations: the
--   settings, the tables generated code refers to by index, and the state
--   below. One per JIT (which is one per process; see JIT.hs).
data Compiler
Compiler :: !Config -> !Exits -> !Frames -> !Pool -> !IORef (Map (Ptr NativeCell) Unit) -> !IORef CompileTotals -> !IORef (Map String AuxMemo) -> !IORef (Map Word64 [Ptr NativeCell]) -> !IORef Int -> Compiler
[cConfig] :: Compiler -> !Config
[cExits] :: Compiler -> !Exits
[cFrames] :: Compiler -> !Frames
[cPool] :: Compiler -> !Pool

-- | Re-entry functions that have a cell but no code yet, by cell. The
--   interpreter counts the times it finds such a cell empty; when the
--   count says the re-entry point is used, the unit is found here and
--   queued for compilation. The cell's request state keeps it from being
--   queued twice.
[cPending] :: Compiler -> !IORef (Map (Ptr NativeCell) Unit)
[cTotals] :: Compiler -> !IORef CompileTotals

-- | the auxiliary functions known for each root function (see
--   <a>uRoot</a>)
[cRootMemos] :: Compiler -> !IORef (Map String AuxMemo)

-- | for each group number, the first cell of every group seen with that
--   number (see <a>groupUnits</a>)
[cGroupCells] :: Compiler -> !IORef (Map Word64 [Ptr NativeCell])

-- | numbers the private copies, so that their symbols are unique in the
--   process (a group's own names are unique, a copy of it can be made by
--   several modules)
[cCopyCounter] :: Compiler -> !IORef Int
newCompiler :: Config -> IO Compiler

-- | What compilation needs, found once at startup.
data JITState
JITState :: Layouts -> CtxOffsets -> RtsFacts -> JITState
[jsLayouts] :: JITState -> Layouts
[jsCtx] :: JITState -> CtxOffsets
[jsRts] :: JITState -> RtsFacts

-- | One LLVM function to generate, with what it brings along: a
--   combinator, or a re-entry function that was left for later.
data Unit
unitName :: Unit -> String

-- | The units of one top-level definition: those to compile now, and those
--   to compile when they turn out to be used. Entry points and local
--   functions (zero in the low bits of their number) are compiled now. A
--   Let body combinator is a re-entry point, entered only through the cell
--   its Let carries when the Let's binding left native code: when
--   <tt>lazy</tt>, it waits until that has happened often enough. Let body
--   combinators that no Let refers to (the ones inside bindings) are never
--   entered.
--   
--   Function names must be unique in the process, and group numbers aren't
--   when a second runtime (with a code cache of its own) is started: the
--   names of a group whose number has been seen with different cells get a
--   suffix.
groupUnits :: Compiler -> Bool -> Bool -> Reference -> Word64 -> MCombs -> IO ([Unit], [Unit])

-- | Private copies of a compiled group's entry point and local functions,
--   for a module that calls them (see <a>uCopy</a>). The group's re-entry
--   points are not the copy's business: the Lets' cells belong to the
--   group and were dealt with when it was compiled.
copyUnits :: Compiler -> Bool -> Reference -> Word64 -> MCombs -> IO [Unit]

-- | Compiles some units as one module and installs the code in their
--   cells. Units that aren't worth compiling (see JIT.Estimate) or that
--   the code generator can't handle are left interpreted, and are not
--   asked for again: a cell's count reaches zero once. When <tt>lazy</tt>,
--   the re-entry functions that are only needed when something exits are
--   not generated: they become pending units (see <tt>pending</tt>).
compileUnits :: Compiler -> JITState -> EnumMap Word64 Reference -> String -> Bool -> [Unit] -> IO ()
addPending :: Compiler -> Unit -> IO ()
lookupPending :: Compiler -> Ptr NativeCell -> IO (Maybe Unit)

-- | Forgets a unit that has been dealt with.
dropPending :: Compiler -> Unit -> IO ()

-- | What has been compiled so far, for <tt>UNISON_JIT_STATS</tt>.
data CompileTotals
CompileTotals :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> CompileTotals

-- | modules handed to LLVM
[ctModules] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | functions for combinators, auxiliary functions generated with them,
--   and re-entry functions generated later, on demand
[ctFunctions] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | functions for combinators, auxiliary functions generated with them,
--   and re-entry functions generated later, on demand
[ctAuxiliary] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | functions for combinators, auxiliary functions generated with them,
--   and re-entry functions generated later, on demand
[ctOnDemand] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | private copies of compiled callees (see <a>uCopy</a>)
[ctCopies] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | re-entry functions still waiting to be asked for
[ctPending] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | functions left to the interpreter because native code for them would
--   mostly exit (see JIT.Estimate)
[ctNotWorthIt] :: CompileTotals -> !Int
[ctIRBytes] :: CompileTotals -> !Int

-- | time spent in all, and of that: generating the IR (judging the units,
--   both passes of the generator, the text), in LLVM's parser and
--   optimizer (<tt>addModule</tt>), and in its code generator (the
--   lookups, since LLJIT compiles a module when its first symbol is looked
--   up)
[ctNanoseconds] :: CompileTotals -> !Word64

-- | time spent in all, and of that: generating the IR (judging the units,
--   both passes of the generator, the text), in LLVM's parser and
--   optimizer (<tt>addModule</tt>), and in its code generator (the
--   lookups, since LLJIT compiles a module when its first symbol is looked
--   up)
[ctGenerate] :: CompileTotals -> !Word64

-- | time spent in all, and of that: generating the IR (judging the units,
--   both passes of the generator, the text), in LLVM's parser and
--   optimizer (<tt>addModule</tt>), and in its code generator (the
--   lookups, since LLJIT compiles a module when its first symbol is looked
--   up)
[ctOptimize] :: CompileTotals -> !Word64

-- | time spent in all, and of that: generating the IR (judging the units,
--   both passes of the generator, the text), in LLVM's parser and
--   optimizer (<tt>addModule</tt>), and in its code generator (the
--   lookups, since LLJIT compiles a module when its first symbol is looked
--   up)
[ctCodegen] :: CompileTotals -> !Word64
compileTotals :: Compiler -> IO CompileTotals


-- | The JIT's entry points for the rest of the runtime, and the handle
--   that holds its state. See
--   unison-runtime<i>src</i>Unison<i>Runtime</i>JIT/design.md.
module Unison.Runtime.JIT

-- | The JIT: its settings and everything it keeps while the process runs.
--   There is one per process, made by ucm at startup (<a>newJIT</a>) and
--   given to every runtime it starts, since what the JIT compiles is
--   shared: generated code refers to the exits and frames tables and the
--   constant pool by index, and native code in one module calls into
--   another directly. Each code cache carries the handle (CCache's
--   <tt>jit</tt>), which is how the interpreter reaches it.
data JIT

-- | A JIT with these settings, not started: nothing is loaded or compiled
--   until <a>loadJIT</a> or <a>startJIT</a>. In the off mode it is inert,
--   and the runtime's calls into it return at once.
newJIT :: Config -> IO JIT

-- | The type reference each type number stands for, as the cache numbers
--   them.
typeNumbers :: JIT -> IO (EnumMap Word64 Reference)

-- | Reads the settings from the environment. Called once, by ucm at
--   startup, after the <tt>--jit</tt> options have been put in the
--   environment.
readConfig :: IO Config
jitConfig :: JIT -> Config
jitExits :: JIT -> Exits
jitFrames :: JIT -> Frames
jitPool :: JIT -> Pool

-- | Whether every transition between native code and the interpreter is
--   logged (<tt>UNISON_JIT_TRACE</tt>).
jitTracing :: JIT -> Bool

-- | Whether entries and exits are counted (<tt>UNISON_JIT_STATS</tt>).
jitStats :: JIT -> Bool

-- | The count a combinator's cell starts with: minus the threshold in the
--   <tt>on</tt> mode, zero (never hot) otherwise.
initialNativeCount :: JIT -> Int

-- | The slots a fresh Unison stack has: the stress mode <tt>ustack=N</tt>
--   makes it tiny, so that growing the stack is exercised constantly.
stackSlots :: JIT -> Int

-- | Loads LLVM at startup, when the JIT is turned on, and says how it
--   went: Nothing when the JIT is off, otherwise whether it is activated,
--   and if not, lines explaining why. Whatever the answer, the program
--   runs: without the JIT everything is interpreted.
loadJIT :: JIT -> IO (Maybe (Either [String] String))

-- | Gets the JIT going if it is enabled. Called by each runtime as it
--   starts. LLVM is normally loaded already, by <a>loadJIT</a> at ucm's
--   startup; if not (another host of the runtime), eager mode loads it
--   here and <tt>on</tt> mode on the compile thread, when the first
--   request arrives.
startJIT :: JIT -> IO ()

-- | Compiles a freshly loaded top-level definition, in eager mode.
jitCompileGroup :: JIT -> Bool -> Reference -> Word64 -> MCombs -> IO ()

-- | Asks for the definition this combinator belongs to to be compiled.
--   Called by the interpreter when the combinator's call count says it is
--   hot (see <a>bumpNativeCount</a>). If the queue is full the flag is
--   cleared again and the count set to ask again after another 1024 calls.
--   The cache's combinators and their references are given as the TVars,
--   read again on the compile thread when the request is served.
jitRequestGroup :: JIT -> Bool -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 MCombs) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference) -> CombIx -> Ptr NativeCell -> IO ()

-- | Asks for the re-entry function that belongs in this cell to be
--   generated, if there is one waiting (see <a>pending</a>). Called by the
--   interpreter when it has found the cell empty often enough. The cell's
--   request state keeps it from being queued twice.
jitRequestCell :: JIT -> Ptr NativeCell -> IO ()

-- | The trampoline's report of an ad hoc exit (the poll, the allocation
--   budget, stack growth: <a>isAdHoc</a>) that unwound through a Let whose
--   body has no code yet. The exits the code itself causes count toward
--   the body's re-entry function when its frame is popped
--   (Machine.countReentry) and are bounded by the code; these land
--   wherever the program is, so a long-running function would in time be
--   interrupted at every Let it has and get a copy of its suffix after
--   each. So they count here, and only while the group's budget lasts
--   (<a>reentryAdHoc</a>, 3): the Lets most often on the stack at a tick,
--   where the time goes, are the ones that get in. The frame the
--   trampoline builds for such an exit carries no cell, so the pop
--   interprets the body without counting it again.
noteAdHocExit :: JIT -> Word64 -> Ptr NativeCell -> IO ()

-- | Records the type numbering of the code cache. Called when types are
--   numbered: for the builtins at startup, and whenever code is loaded.
registerTypeNumbers :: JIT -> EnumMap Word64 Reference -> IO ()

-- | Prints how often each exit was taken, when UNISON_JIT_STATS is set.
--   Called after each evaluation.
printJITStats :: JIT -> IO ()

-- | Called by the interpreter after each foreign call. With
--   <tt>UNISON_JIT_STATS=each</tt>, a call that wrote output is followed
--   by the exits taken since the program last wrote (the busiest sites
--   only), after which counting starts again; so a program that prints a
--   line per phase gets its exits listed per phase.
noteOutput :: JIT -> ForeignFunc -> IO ()

module Unison.Runtime.Machine.Types
type Tick = CombIx -> K -> IO ()
type Tag = Word64

-- | A ref storing every currently active thread. This is helpful for
--   cleaning up orphaned threads when the main process completes.
--   
--   We track threads when running in a host process like UCM, otherwise,
--   in one-off environments <a>Nothing</a> is used and we don't bother
--   tracking forked threads since they'll be cleaned up automatically on
--   process termination.
type ActiveThreads = Maybe IORef Set ThreadId
data CCache prof
CCache :: Bool -> (Bool -> Val -> Tracer) -> !prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Combs) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 MCombs) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference) -> TVar (EnumSet Word64) -> TVar (OptInfos Reference Symbol) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference) -> TVar Word64 -> TVar Word64 -> TVar Word64 -> TVar (Map Reference (SuperGroup Reference Symbol)) -> TVar (Map Reference Word64) -> TVar (Map Reference Word64) -> TVar (BiMap RecordSchema RecordRef) -> TVar (Map Reference (Set Reference)) -> TVar RecordFieldMappings -> TVar NativeCellPool -> {-# NOUNPACK #-} !JIT -> CCache prof
[sandboxed] :: CCache prof -> Bool
[tracer] :: CCache prof -> Bool -> Val -> Tracer
[profiler] :: CCache prof -> !prof
[srcCombs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Combs)
[combs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 MCombs)
[combRefs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference)
[cacheableCombs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumSet Word64)
[optInfos] :: CCache prof -> TVar (OptInfos Reference Symbol)
[tagRefs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference)
[freshTm] :: CCache prof -> TVar Word64
[freshTy] :: CCache prof -> TVar Word64
[freshRecSchema] :: CCache prof -> TVar Word64
[intermed] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference (SuperGroup Reference Symbol))
[refTm] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference Word64)
[refTy] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference Word64)
[recordRefs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (BiMap RecordSchema RecordRef)
[sandbox] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference (Set Reference))
[recordFieldMappings] :: CCache prof -> TVar RecordFieldMappings
[nativeCells] :: CCache prof -> TVar NativeCellPool
[jit] :: CCache prof -> {-# NOUNPACK #-} !JIT
type Combs = GCombs Void CombIx
data Tracer
NoTrace :: Tracer
MsgTrace :: String -> String -> String -> Tracer
SimpleTrace :: String -> Tracer
baseCCache :: JIT -> Bool -> IO (CCache ())

-- | How many native code cells a fresh cache starts with. Each is 16
--   bytes.
initialNativeCells :: Int
refLookup :: String -> Map Reference Word64 -> Reference -> Word64
refNumTm :: CCache prof -> Reference -> IO Word64
refNumsTm :: CCache prof -> IO (Map Reference Word64)
refNumsTy :: CCache prof -> IO (Map Reference Word64)
recordRefLookup :: BiMap RecordSchema RecordRef -> RecordSchema -> RecordRef
class RuntimeProfiler prof where {
    data Ticker prof;
}
startTicker :: RuntimeProfiler prof => prof -> IO (Ticker prof, IO ())
checkTicker :: RuntimeProfiler prof => Ticker prof -> CombIx -> K -> IO ()
data family Ticker prof
tickCallback :: Int -> (Bool -> Tick) -> IORef (Maybe Tick) -> IORef Bool -> IO ()
lookupCode :: CCache prof -> Referent -> IO (Maybe (Referenced Code))
resolveCode :: Reference -> Map Reference (SuperGroup Reference Symbol) -> Map Reference Word64 -> EnumSet Word64 -> Maybe (Code Reference)
canonicalizeCodeRefs :: Code Reference -> IO (Referenced Code)
cacheability :: Map Reference Word64 -> EnumSet Word64 -> Reference -> Cacheability
checkSandboxing :: CCache prof -> [Reference] -> Closure -> IO Bool
checkValueSandboxing :: CCache prof -> [Reference] -> Value Reference -> IO (Either [Referent] [Referent])
codeValidate :: CCache prof -> [(Reference, SuperGroup Reference Symbol)] -> IO (Maybe (Failure Text))

-- | The code the interpreter runs: MCode over resolved combinators and
--   these values. (Defined here, below the JIT modules, so that the JIT
--   handle can be a field of the code cache without an import cycle.)
type MCombs = RCombs Val
type MSection = RSection Val
type MBranch = RBranch Val
type MInstr = RInstr Val
type MComb = RComb Val
type MRef = RRef Val
instance Unison.Runtime.Machine.Types.RuntimeProfiler Unison.Runtime.Profiling.ProfileComm
instance Unison.Runtime.Machine.Types.RuntimeProfiler ()

module Unison.Runtime.Machine

-- | A ref storing every currently active thread. This is helpful for
--   cleaning up orphaned threads when the main process completes.
--   
--   We track threads when running in a host process like UCM, otherwise,
--   in one-off environments <a>Nothing</a> is used and we don't bother
--   tracking forked threads since they'll be cleaned up automatically on
--   process termination.
type ActiveThreads = Maybe IORef Set ThreadId
data CCache prof
CCache :: Bool -> (Bool -> Val -> Tracer) -> !prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Combs) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 MCombs) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference) -> TVar (EnumSet Word64) -> TVar (OptInfos Reference Symbol) -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference) -> TVar Word64 -> TVar Word64 -> TVar Word64 -> TVar (Map Reference (SuperGroup Reference Symbol)) -> TVar (Map Reference Word64) -> TVar (Map Reference Word64) -> TVar (BiMap RecordSchema RecordRef) -> TVar (Map Reference (Set Reference)) -> TVar RecordFieldMappings -> TVar NativeCellPool -> {-# NOUNPACK #-} !JIT -> CCache prof
[sandboxed] :: CCache prof -> Bool
[tracer] :: CCache prof -> Bool -> Val -> Tracer
[profiler] :: CCache prof -> !prof
[srcCombs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Combs)
[combs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 MCombs)
[combRefs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference)
[cacheableCombs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumSet Word64)
[optInfos] :: CCache prof -> TVar (OptInfos Reference Symbol)
[tagRefs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (EnumMap Word64 Reference)
[freshTm] :: CCache prof -> TVar Word64
[freshTy] :: CCache prof -> TVar Word64
[freshRecSchema] :: CCache prof -> TVar Word64
[intermed] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference (SuperGroup Reference Symbol))
[refTm] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference Word64)
[refTy] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference Word64)
[recordRefs] :: CCache prof -> TVar (BiMap RecordSchema RecordRef)
[sandbox] :: CCache prof -> TVar (Map Reference (Set Reference))
[recordFieldMappings] :: CCache prof -> TVar RecordFieldMappings
[nativeCells] :: CCache prof -> TVar NativeCellPool
[jit] :: CCache prof -> {-# NOUNPACK #-} !JIT
type Combs = GCombs Void CombIx

NoTrace :: Tracer

--   bytes.

module Unison.Runtime.Interface
startRuntime :: JIT -> Bool -> RuntimeHost -> Text -> IO (Runtime Symbol)
withRuntime :: MonadUnliftIO m => JIT -> Bool -> RuntimeHost -> Text -> (Runtime Symbol -> m a) -> m a
standalone :: CCache () -> Word64 -> IO StoredCache
runStandalone :: JIT -> Bool -> StoredCache -> CombIx -> IO (Either Error ())

-- | A version of the Code Cache designed to be serialized to disk as
--   standalone bytecode.
data StoredCache
SCache :: EnumMap Word64 Combs -> EnumMap Word64 Reference -> EnumSet Word64 -> OptInfos Reference Symbol -> EnumMap Word64 Reference -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Map Reference (SuperGroup Reference Symbol) -> Map Reference Word64 -> Map Reference Word64 -> BiMap RecordSchema RecordRef -> Map Reference (Set Reference) -> RecordFieldMappings -> Replacements -> StoredCache
decodeStandalone :: ByteString -> IO (Either String (Text, Text, CombIx, StoredCache))

-- | Whether the runtime is hosted within a persistent session or as a
--   one-off process. This affects the amount of clean-up and book-keeping
--   the runtime does.
data RuntimeHost
OneOff :: RuntimeHost
Persistent :: RuntimeHost
type Runtime = Runtime Error DecompError
terminate :: Runtime e e' v -> IO ()
getStoredCache :: forall (m :: Type -> Type). PrimBase m => Get m StoredCache
putStoredCache :: StoredCache -> Builder

-- | <b>NB</b>: The only reason this is in the unison-runtime package is
--   because it’s used in the tests. Otherwise it should move to
--   unison-cli.
prettyError :: Applicative f => (Word -> f (Pretty ColorText)) -> Error -> f (Pretty ColorText)
prettyRuntimeExn :: Applicative f => (Word -> f (Pretty ColorText)) -> RuntimeExn -> f (Pretty ColorText)
renderDecompError :: DecompError -> Pretty ColorText
tabulateErrors :: Set DecompError -> Pretty ColorText
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Unison.Runtime.Interface.StoredCache
instance (GHC.Classes.Ord from, GHC.Classes.Ord to) => GHC.Internal.Base.Monoid (Unison.Runtime.Interface.Remapping from to)
instance (GHC.Classes.Ord from, GHC.Classes.Ord to) => GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup (Unison.Runtime.Interface.Remapping from to)
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Unison.Runtime.Interface.StoredCache

module Unison.Runtime.Vector
data Vec a
[Scalar] :: forall a. a -> Vec a
[Vec] :: forall a. Unbox a => Vector a -> Vec a
[Pair] :: forall a1 b. Vec a1 -> Vec b -> Vec (a1, b)
[Choose] :: forall a. Vec Bool -> Vec a -> Vec a -> Vec a
[Mux] :: forall a. Vec Nat -> Vec (Vec a) -> Vec a
type Nat = Word64
mu :: Vec a -> Nat -> Maybe a
bound :: Nat -> Vec a -> Nat
toList :: Vec a -> [a]
